descripcion_geo: Inner region of Asia Minor between Pisidia and Cappadocia. Main cities: Lystra, Iconium and Derbe.

historias.titulo: Paul and Barnabas worshiped as gods at Lystra
historias.descripcion: After healing a lame man in Lystra, the Lycaonians believe they are Zeus and Hermes; Paul tears their clothes to dissuade them.
Jews from Antioch and Iconium convince the Lycaonians; Paul is stoned and dragged out of the city.

historias.titulo: Timothy son of Lystra of Lycaonia
historias.descripcion: Timothy, a disciple of Paul, was born in Lystra of Lycaonia; His mother Eunice and grandmother Loida had transmitted the faith to him.

personajes.descripcion: He was worshiped as a god and then stoned in Lystra of Lycaonia; the maximum contrast of the mission.
Natural of Lystra of Lycaonia; companion and favorite disciple of Paul.
Mistaken for Zeus at Lystra; evangelized the region with Paul.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Lycaonia: relevant region in the NT world.

cristianismo.descripcion: The Lystra episode reveals the religious confusion of paganism and the apostolic reaction: the missionaries are not gods but messengers of the living God.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The Lystra episode reveals the religious confusion of paganism and the apostolic reaction: the missionaries are not gods but messengers of the living God.
